articles.title: Odisha Rains: Heavy downpour lashes parts of state, schools closed in THESE districts; IMD issues alert - India.com
articles.full_text:
New Delhi: Owing to heavy rainfall in Odisha, the Mohan Charan Majhi government has ordered the closure of schools in two districts of the state. Flash floods were also reported along the embankments of the Hati River in Odisha’s Kalahandi district on Sunday amid heavy rainfall triggered by a low-pressure system.
Under the impact of the low-pressure area in northwestern Bay of Bengal, heavy rainfall is expected in several districts of Odisha till August 26, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
Authorities released 412 cusecs of water from the Mangalpur Barrage of the Indravati Project into Hati River, which was already in spate, causing flash floods in its embankments this morning, officials said.
Floodwaters entered low-lying areas of Talpada, Bankapala and Jampadar villages under Kalampur block. The block administration, led by BDO Vijay Kumar Marandi, rescued 293 people from both Paruaguda and Bodelbandh villages and provided them with free ration, an official said.
Road communication from Junagarh to Kalampur and Thuamul Rampur Road to Kashipur has been disrupted due to heavy rain. In view of the rainfall forecast, district administrations have announced that all schools and anganwadi centres in Nabarangpur, and 89 schools in vulnerable areas of Bhadrak would remain closed on Monday.
Several areas in the state received heavy to extreme heavy downpour in the last 24 hours till 8.30 this morning. Of those, at least two places recorded over 200 mm of rainfall. Thuamula Rampur in Kalahandi district recorded extreme heavy rainfall of 345 mm, while Kashipur in Rayagada district received 212 mm of downpour, the weather office said.
Nineteen other places recorded between 100 mm and 200 mm of rainfall in the last 24 hours, it said.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over the Bay of Bengal off the West Bengal-Bangladesh coasts intensified into a low-pressure area during early Sunday morning, the IMD said. The system is likely to move northwestwards across north Odisha adjoining Gangetic West Bengal in the next 24 hours, it said.
The weather office also issued an ‘orange’ warning (be prepared to take action) for Sundergarh, Jharsuguda, Bargarh, Sambalpur, Sonepur, and Boudh districts for Monday.
Similarly, a ‘yellow warning’ (be aware) has been issued for Balasore, Deogarh, Anugul, Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj, Nuapada, Bolangir, Kalahandi, Kandhamal, Nawarangpur, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati, Ganjam, and Nayagada.
Thunderstorms, accompanied by lightning and gusty surface wind, are expected in many other places across Odisha, the IMD said.
